summary: Practise risk screening, supplier engagement, and remediation using UNGPs and OECD guidance. Explore the course and build practical due-diligence skills.
lede: Human rights due diligence is an ongoing process for identifying, preventing, mitigating and accounting for impacts. For ESG, procurement, legal, compliance, lending and safeguards professionals, the course applies it to decisions across operations and business relationships. Participants practise risk screening, severity-based prioritization, supplier engagement, remediation tracking and evidence-based reporting, including AI-assisted adverse-media screening with human review.
audienceIntro: This course is designed for professionals who make, review, or report decisions about human-rights impacts in operations, lending, procurement, and development programmes.
audience: Lender Environmental and Social Risk Officers
prerequisites: Working familiarity with ESG, procurement, human-rights, legal and compliance, lending, or safeguards processes is recommended. Coding is not required. For the digital screening exercise, bring a laptop with access to Microsoft Excel or an equivalent spreadsheet application; no specialist screening platform is required.
